**Answer: Yes, $\|f\|_{E'} \leq c$.**

**Proof.**

Recall that the weak-star topology on $E'$ is the topology of pointwise convergence on $E$: $f_n \to f$ in the weak-star topology means $f_n(x) \to f(x)$ for every $x \in E$.

The dual norm is given by
$$\|g\|_{E'} = \sup_{\|x\|_E \leq 1} |g(x)|.$$

Fix any $x \in E$ with $\|x\|_E \leq 1$. Since $f_n \to f$ weak-star, we have $f_n(x) \to f(x)$, hence $|f_n(x)| \to |f(x)|$. By hypothesis, $\|f_n\|_{E'} \leq c$ for all $n$, so for every $n$,
$$|f_n(x)| \leq \|f_n\|_{E'} \leq c.$$

Taking the limit as $n \to \infty$ (limits preserve non-strict inequalities),
$$|f(x)| = \lim_{n \to \infty} |f_n(x)| \leq c.$$

This holds for every $x$ with $\|x\|_E \leq 1$. Taking the supremum over all such $x$,
$$\|f\|_{E'} = \sup_{\|x\|_E \leq 1} |f(x)| \leq c.$$

$\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
